Subject: DTIA scope for Medixa pilot — SCCs + UK Addendum

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving to a small pilot (production-lite) in Q1 and our legal team has asked us to lock down the DTIA/TIA scope up front so we can feed it into procurement. The pilot will process UK customer PII and EU member-state data; Medixa needs assurance that the international transfer controls are documented (SCCs + UK Addendum where needed) and that subprocessors are enumerated.

Could Redwood confirm:
- Whether the standard SCCs bundle you use is preceded by the UK IDTA or whether we need a separate UK Addendum;
- A shortlist of subprocessors involved (or a plan to provide the mapping and timing);
- What evidence/artefacts you can provide for the TIA (data flow diagram, encryption notes, retention controls, subprocessors CSV).

We can share our TIA template if useful. Ideally we'd get a scoped DTIA (one-pager) and an evidence packet for the pilot by end of month so procurement can start drafting the SOW.

Thanks,

Thomas Blythe

Thomas — thanks, and congrats on getting to pilot. High level: Redwood will support SCCs for EU transfers and the UK IDTA/UK Addendum where the data flow includes UK-resident data. We treat those as complementary: we can provide the SCC module plus the UK Addendum text for the UK jurisdiction.

Immediate ask from our side so we can scope the DTIA:
- Confirm which datasets in the pilot are UK-resident (fields/examples) and whether there are any clinical identifiers beyond standard PII;
- Confirm whether Medixa will require on-prem for log retention or if cloud storage with KMS-managed keys is acceptable;
- Approve Redwood sharing a linked subprocessors CSV and a short evidence pack (dataflow diagram, encryption-at-rest/in-transit notes, retention table).

I attached our DTIA checklist and the current subprocessors export (redacted for vendor contact). Laura/Vivek/Olga — can you weigh in on the TIA artefact list and whether we need a practice-level PIA for the pilot?

Next steps suggested: we prepare a 1-page DTIA + evidence packet and send to Medixa legal for review by 2026-11-30. If procurement wants a bespoke UK Addendum sign-off, we can loop Legal for redlines.

Thanks — talk soon.

Regards,

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 11:03 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thomas — thanks, and congrats on getting to pilot. High level: Redwood will support SCCs for EU transfers and the UK IDTA/UK Addendum where the data flow includes UK-resident data.

Couple of technical clarifications and proposed evidence list from infra/ops: 

1) Subprocessors: we'll provide the current subprocessors CSV (attached) with a timestamp and we will notify Medixa of any material changes with a 30-day notice during the pilot. For this pilot the likely subprocessors touching data are: GCP (compute/storage), RedisCloud (cache), and a managed logging provider (Logflare). We'll mark which subprocessors handle encrypted raw payloads vs. tokenized metadata.

2) SCCs/UK Addendum handling: Redwood publishes a standard SCC module we attach by default; for UK-resident personal data we attach the UK Addendum and include an Annex mapping the UK Addendum to the SCC clauses. That Annex will live in the evidence packet.

3) TIA artefacts we can deliver for pilot: data-flow diagram (SVG/PDF), description of transfer mechanisms, crypto summary (TLS + AES-256 at rest, with KMS key IDs redacted), retention schedule table, subprocessors CSV, and an operational runbook excerpt showing how we purge cached KV entries on request. We cannot share HSM key material but can provide KMS logs sample.

4) PIA/PIA-lite: given this is a narrowly scoped pilot, propose a PIA-lite (2 pages) that references the DTIA and enumerates residual risk & mitigations. That should satisfy procurement for pilot SOW.

Deliverable timeline: Redwood prepares 1-page DTIA + evidence zip by 2026-11-30; Medixa legal reviews and provides redlines by 2026-12-07; procurement drafts SOW by 2026-12-14.

If that works, we'll prepare the artefacts and share a Drive link.

—Laura
